subject: Dedicated single-tenant pricing and compliance premium — Stellate Systems
messages:
From: Maria Rossi <maria.rossi@stellate.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stellate.ai, Jason Li <jason.li@stellate.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated single-tenant requirement / KMS & audit logging (RFP attached)

Hi Hannah,

Following up on our brief at the conference — Stellate is evaluating a dedicated single-tenant deployment for Q4. Key asks:
- GPU pool: sizing for 4 x A100-equivalent nodes (primarily generation workloads, median seq len ~512)
- Throughput & latency guarantees (99th pctl target <150ms for interactive calls)
- Compliance: customer-managed KMS, audit log retention (5 years), SOC2 evidence and quarterly access reviews
- Commercial: committed reserved pricing (12/24/36 mo) and isolation premium for single-tenant option; procurement will need discount bands and cancellation language

Can you send a baseline commercial (ballpark) and any sizing worksheet we should fill? Attached is our short RFP to speed things up. Looking to close by end of September.

Best,
Maria
Maria Rossi
Head of Infrastructure, Stellate Systems
Attachments: RFP_stellate_q3.pdf (PDF, 420KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maria Rossi <maria.rossi@stellate.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated single-tenant requirement / KMS & audit logging (RFP attached)

Maria — thanks for the RFP and the clear requirements. High level answer below and I attached a sizing template for you to populate.

Ballpark commercial (monthly, USD, per 4-node pool):
- Base Dedicated (multi-tenant baseline price): $85,000 / month
- Single-tenant isolation premium (KMS + dedicated audit/log pipeline + tenant-level isolation): +22%
- Commit discounts (applied to base+premium): 12 mo = 10% | 24 mo = 16% | 36 mo = 22%

Notes & variables:
- SLA/throughput guarantees are priced to capacity. To meet 99th <150ms at 1k concurrent interactive sessions we typically reserve headroom ( GPUs pinned, no noisy neighbors). If you want hard 99th SLOs we add a 10–18% availability margin depending on seq length distribution.
- KMS: integration with customer-managed KMS adds operational setup and an ongoing HSM fee; we list it as part of the premium but can break it out on the contract.

Please complete the attached Redwood_Dedicated_Sizing_Template.xlsx with expected concurrent sessions, average/95th/99th seq lengths, and desired retention window for logs. With that we can produce a firm price and a Mutual Action Plan.

Next step: 30-min sizing call Thursday or Friday? I’ve CC'd Ben (SE) and Jordan (Manager, pricing approvals).

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Sizing_Template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Maria Rossi <maria.rossate@stellate.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Sep 2025 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated single-tenant requirement / KMS & audit logging (technical sizing notes)

Maria / team — following up from our call. A few technical clarifications that materially affect cost:

1) Workload shape & tail: 99th latency is highly sensitive to peak burstiness and seq length. If you have a small fraction (<5%) of long-context (>2k) sessions, we need larger KV cache sizing and more headroom.

2) Throughput guidance for 4x A100-equivalent (gen workloads, seq ~512):
- Sustained throughput (tokens/s): ~18k–22k tokens/s across the pool
- Concurrent interactive sessions (median): ~1,200 comfortably; 99th pctl latency target of 150ms requires reserving ~25% headroom vs peak observed

3) SLO proposal (firm):
- Availability: 99.5% monthly
- Latency: 99th pctl <150ms for calls <1s compute time (excludes network) — subject to request size limits or burst queueing
- Remedy: SLA credits scaling to 20% of monthly invoice for repeated missed SLOs (standard cap)

4) Cost levers that reduce premium:
- Prefix/KV caching on customer side — can cut token cost by ~12%
- Quantized model variants for non-critical traffic — additional ~5–8% savings

I attached a short runbook describing how throughput maps to GPU count. Happy to run a quick synthetic test if you can share a 24–48 hour sample trace.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: throughput_runbook.pdf (doc)

From: Maria Rossi <maria.rossi@stellate.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Li <jason.li@stellate.ai>, procurement@stellate.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated single-tenant requirement / KMS & audit logging (RFP attached)

Thanks Hannah and Ben — the technical notes are helpful. A few commercial counterpoints from our procurement/legal team: 

1) Isolation premium: 22% on top of the base is higher than we expected. For a 24-month committed spend we would expect the premium capped at 15%.
2) Ramp window & remedies: we want a 3-month ramp with a partial refund if throughput targets are not met (pro-rata credit on committed spend).
3) Onboarding credit: request a one-time credit to offset migration effort (typically 10–15% of first-year spend).
4) Standard procurement asks: net-60 term (we budget on 60 day), termination for material breach, and a mutual non-solicit.

Attached is our procurement template with the clauses we need highlighted. Can Redwood share a proposed redline if the price and ramp can be adjusted?

Best,
Maria
Attachments: stellate_net_terms.docx (Word)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Maria Rossi <maria.rossate@stellate.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated single-tenant requirement / KMS & audit logging (pricing response)

Maria — thanks for the feedback and the procurement template. We want to be flexible and keep this moving. Proposed commercial concessions: 

- Isolation premium: Redwood will cap the single-tenant premium at 15% provided Stellate signs a 24-month committed usage agreement and hits a minimum utilization threshold (80% of reserved monthly capacity).
- Ramp & refund: 3-month ramp window accepted. If Redwood fails to meet the agreed throughput SLOs during the ramp month, we will provide a pro-rata credit up to 25% of that month's invoice (one-time on-boarding protection).
- One-time onboarding credit: Redwood will provide a $20,000 onboarding credit applied to first invoice.
- Payment terms: we can accept net-45 for a committed enterprise contract (finance prefers net-45 vs net-60). If Stellate requires net-60, we will need to discuss a small financing fee (to be defined).

Legal: Please send your redlines; we will have our legal and finance prepare a counter-redline including the KMS/HSM scope and SLA language. Evelyn will coordinate the contract.

Jordan Blake
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maria Rossi <maria.rossate@stellate.ai>, procurement@stellate.ai
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2025 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated single-tenant requirement / KMS & audit logging — next steps

Maria — great progress, thanks. Summary of agreed commercial points for the Mutual Action Plan:
- 24-mo committed Dedicated (4x A100-equivalent)
- Single-tenant isolation premium capped at 15% (applied to base price)
- 80% utilization minimum; failure to meet leads to standard contract remedies
- 3-month ramp with one-time pro-rata refund up to 25% of a ramp month's invoice for missed SLOs (one-time)
- $20k onboarding credit applied to first invoice
- Payment: net-45 (we noted your net-60 request; will escalate if required)

Attachments: Mutual_Action_Plan_Stellate_Redwood.xlsx, Redwood_Dedicated_SLA_v1.pdf
DocuSign: https://docusign.com/secure/abc123-mutual-action-stellate

Next steps:
1) Stellate to return redlined procurement template (stellate_net_terms.docx) — target Thu 18 Sep
2) Redwood legal to produce contract redline and send DocuSign by Tue 23 Sep
3) KMS onboarding and HSM coordination contact: security-ops@redwood.com (we will assign a PM after signature)

If that matches your expectations I’ll have Evelyn create the MOK (Master Order / PO) placeholder and route for signature.

Thanks again — excited to work with Stellate.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachments: Mutual_Action_Plan_Stellate_Redwood.xlsx (spreadsheet), Redwood_Dedicated_SLA_v1.pdf (PDF)
